messages.subject: Regime Switching and Formula
messages.body_plain:
From: Danilo Brandão

Dear All,
I would like some suggestions on a regime switching model i'm trying to implement. It's a time series model where only my transition equation is regime dependent. Although, when i try to define the noise object i get the following message

"Oi, Chap! I found 1 regime for 'values.observed' but 2 regimes elsewhere, so I extended the observed covariances to match.
If this is what you wanted, all is sunshine and puppy dogs."

Another issue that i encoutered is how to implement formulas in the factor loading matrix as in the spirit of Nelson-Siegel models form term structure(Levant & Ma(2016); Caldeira(2016) and others)

Thanks for your attention

--
Michael D. Hunter, PhD
Assistant Professor of Quantitative Psychology
Georgia Institute of Technology
J.S. Coon Building, Room 225
E-mail: mhunt...@gmail.com or mhun...@gatech.edu

messages.subject: Re: Regime Switching and Formula
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your feedback!

The error message is not an error; it's a warning.  It's just saying that it found a non-regime switching part of the model and made it the same across all the regimes.  If that's what you wanted it to do, then everything is fine.

For the formulas with the factor loadings matrix, we have something similar with the prep.loadings() function.  See ?prep.loadings for a bunch of examples.

Best,
Mike Hunter
